$comment: templates/index.json -- the scaffold template pack's table of contents, and the ONE place the template set is written down. It sits beside profiles/ for the same reason profiles/index.json does: a template is DATA, versioned with nen, so that src/scaffold/ carries no toolchain name and a reviewer can read every byte nen would write without reading a single line of TypeScript.
$naming: A template is named by the pack's own `scaffoldTemplate` value (profiles/<stack>.json), never by a stack id -- one template serves every stack the pack points at it, and a stack whose `scaffoldTemplate` is null has no template at all. src/scaffold/templates.test.ts asserts both directions against the pack, so a stack that gains a template name and no directory fails the build rather than a user's scaffold.
$bundling: Each entry below is a directory holding one `template.json`, named in an explicit static import list in src/scaffold/templates.ts -- `bun build --compile` embeds what a static import names and cannot follow a directory read. That list is pinned against this file and against the directory listing in src/scaffold/templates.test.ts.
$placeholders: A template body substitutes `{{token}}` and NOTHING else -- PLACEHOLDER is `{{` + `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*` + `}}`, immediately closed (src/scaffold/templates.ts) -- and an unsupplied token is refused at exit 2 naming it (that module's `substitute`). `${{env.X}}` does NOT match this grammar (the `.` before `}}` breaks the token), so `substitute()` leaves it untouched rather than refusing it; this is a readability guideline, not a refusal rule. Write a GitHub Actions expression with a space -- `${{ env.X }}`, never `${{env.X}}` -- because unspaced it sits one character from `{{token}}` and a reviewer skimming a generated workflow can misread which grammar they are looking at. The bodies below use `${VAR}` inside `run:` scripts for exactly this reason.

minimumNenRef.why: the first release that carries `nen shu` -- every CI body in this pack runs `nen shu tools`, `nen shu build`, `nen shu test` and `nen shu lint`, and none of those verbs exists in v0.2.0 or v0.1.0 (CHANGELOG.md announces the family under `## Unreleased`). A workflow pinned below this ref is red twice over: `bash nen-bootstrap.sh --ref <older>` exits 6 before any verb runs when the tag carries no published release, and a binary that did come back would not have the verbs. `nen scaffold` therefore writes the GREATER of this ref and the running build's own `v${VERSION}`, and refuses a `--nen-ref` below it by name.
